industries.industry: B2B SaaS, Cloud Infrastructure & AI Application Vendors
industries.enterprise_msa_limits: $2M–$5M Combined Tech E&O & Cyber Liability + $1M/$2M CGL
mandatory_endorsements: Combined Technology Errors & Omissions + Network Security/Privacy Liability (eliminates grey-area disputes between software bug vs. security exploit)
Software Copyright / IP & Media Liability Carve-In (essential for generative AI & SaaS codebases)
Breach of Contract / SLA Failure & Contingent Business Interruption (AWS/GCP/Azure upstream outage coverage)
Blanket Additional Insured (ISO CG 20 10 / Tech E&O equivalent) + Primary & Non-Contributory + Waiver of Subrogation
industries.common_coi_trap: Buying standalone General Professional Liability (Hiscox/Next basic tier) without Third-Party Network Security & Privacy coverage — rejected by 94% of Fortune 1000 procurement teams during SOC 2 Type II vendor onboarding.

industries.industry: IT Consultants, Software Dev Agencies & Managed Service Providers (MSPs)
industries.enterprise_msa_limits: $2M–$5M Tech E&O + Third-Party Cyber + $250k Social Engineering
mandatory_endorsements: Vicarious Liability for 1099 Subcontractors & Offshore Developers (must explicitly cover non-W2 contractors)
Third-Party Network Security & Unauthorized Access (covers client network compromise via RMM/VPN credentials)
Defense Costs Outside the Limits (CEOL) or minimum $2M Aggregate so legal fees do not erode indemnification limits
80/20 Soft Hammer Clause (avoids 100% policyholder forfeiture if you reject a premature settlement)
industries.common_coi_trap: Standard policies exclude independent 1099 contractors unless endorsed as 'Insureds' under the policy definition, leaving dev agencies uninsured when a contractor introduces a vulnerability.

industries.industry: FinTech, Payment Facilitators, Bookkeepers & CPA Firms
industries.enterprise_msa_limits: $5M/$5M Financial Institutions E&O + $5M Cyber + $500k Social Engineering / Funds Transfer Fraud
mandatory_endorsements: PCI-DSS Assessments, Card Brand Fines & Forensic Audit Coverage ($250k–$1M sublimit)
Social Engineering, Invoice Manipulation & Funds Transfer Fraud ($250k–$1M sublimit; standard policies cap this at $25k–$100k)
Regulatory Defense & Penalties (CFPB, SEC, NYDFS 23 NYCRR 500, State Money Transmitter / Banking Boards)
Third-Party Commercial Crime / Employee Dishonesty Fidelity Bond
industries.common_coi_trap: Sponsor banks and enterprise CFOs reject COIs where Funds Transfer Fraud / Social Engineering is sublimited below $250,000 or where PCI-DSS fines are excluded under contractual liability.

industries.industry: Digital Health, Healthcare SaaS & HIPAA Business Associates (BAAs)
industries.smb_msa_limits: $1M/$3M Healthcare E&O + $2M Cyber (with HIPAA Regulatory Sublimit)
industries.enterprise_msa_limits: $5M/$5M Cyber & Privacy Liability + $5M Tech E&O (Hospital / Health System BAA Standard)
mandatory_endorsements: HHS OCR HIPAA / HITECH Regulatory Defense & Civil Monetary Penalties Coverage (full policy limit or >= $1M sublimit)
First-Party Patient Breach Notification, Call Center, Forensics & 24-Month Credit Monitoring (outside policy aggregate where available)
Biometric & Health Data Privacy Coverage (covers WA My Health My Data Act & IL BIPA claims unless excluded)
Bodily Injury / Contingent Medical Malpractice Carve-Back (for clinical decision support & telehealth platforms)
industries.common_coi_trap: Standard Tech E&O policies contain an absolute 'Bodily Injury' exclusion that voids coverage if a software bug in a clinical/telehealth workflow allegedly contributes to patient harm.

industries.industry: Federal, State & Defense Government Contractors (FAR / DFARS / CMMC 2.0)
industries.enterprise_msa_limits: $5M/$5M Professional & Cyber Liability + DFARS 252.204-7012 Incident Forensics
mandatory_endorsements: DFARS 252.204-7012 / NIST SP 800-171 72-Hour Cyber Incident Forensic Preservation & Reporting Coverage
Nation-State / Cyber War Attribution Carve-Back (prevents insurer from denying APT attacks under archaic 'Act of War' exclusions)
Government Agency Named as Additional Insured with 30-Day Written Notice of Cancellation
False Claims Act (FCA) Defense Sublimit for cybersecurity self-attestation disputes
industries.common_coi_trap: Legacy Lloyd's/carrier war exclusions (LMA5567 without cyber carve-back) allow insurers to deny state-sponsored APT breaches affecting defense/government suppliers.

industries.smb_msa_limits: $1M Per Claim / $2M Aggregate A&E Professional Liability
industries.enterprise_msa_limits: $2M/$4M to $5M/$5M Practice + Project-Specific E&O + Contractors Pollution Liability
mandatory_endorsements: Faulty Workmanship / Design-Build Professional Liability Carve-Back
Contractors Pollution Liability (CPL) & Mold/Environmental Coverage
3-Year to 5-Year Extended Reporting Period (ERP / Tail Coverage) matching state Statute of Repose
First-Party Wire Fraud / Escrow Manipulation Cyber Coverage for construction draw payments
industries.common_coi_trap: Because A&E E&O is strictly 'Claims-Made', letting a policy lapse after project completion without an Extended Reporting Period (ERP tail) voids coverage for structural defect claims filed years later.

policy_clauses.what_it_means: First-Party covers YOUR direct breach expenses (forensics, ransomware extortion payment, customer notification letters, credit monitoring, business interruption). Third-Party covers lawsuits, enterprise client indemnification demands, and regulatory fines brought AGAINST you.
policy_clauses.contract_standard: Enterprise MSAs require BOTH First-Party Breach Response ($1M–$5M) and Third-Party Network Security & Privacy Liability ($2M–$5M).

policy_clauses.clause: Tech E&O vs. General Professional Liability
policy_clauses.what_it_means: General Professional Liability covers negligent advice or services. Tech E&O specifically adds coverage for software failure to perform as specified in an MSA, SLA downtime, data corruption, and IP/media infringement.
policy_clauses.contract_standard: Any SaaS, AI, or software vendor MUST carry 'Technology E&O' wording—not generic consultant E&O.

policy_clauses.clause: Retroactive Date ('Full Prior Acts' vs. Inception Date)
policy_clauses.what_it_means: E&O and Cyber policies are 'Claims-Made and Reported.' They only cover errors or breaches that occurred ON OR AFTER the policy's Retroactive Date.
policy_clauses.contract_standard: Never accept a reset Retroactive Date when switching carriers; require 'Full Prior Acts' or match your original company incorporation/contract date.

policy_clauses.clause: Defense Inside vs. Outside the Limits (Eroding Policy)
policy_clauses.what_it_means: When defense costs are 'Inside the Limits' (Eroding), every dollar spent on cyber forensics ($400–$950/hr) and defense attorneys reduces the limit available to pay settlements or judgments.
policy_clauses.contract_standard: Request 'Claims Expenses Outside the Limits' (CEOL) or carry an extra $1M–$2M buffer above your largest client MSA minimum.

policy_clauses.what_it_means: If the insurer wants to settle a claim for $300k to save legal fees, and you refuse (to protect your reputation), a '100% Hard Hammer' caps the insurer's payout at $300k and makes you pay 100% of excess defense and judgment costs.
policy_clauses.contract_standard: Insist on an '80/20' or '90/10' Soft Hammer Clause so the carrier still pays 80%–90% of excess defense/settlement costs.

policy_clauses.clause: Social Engineering, Phishing & Funds Transfer Fraud Sublimit
policy_clauses.what_it_means: Covers losses when an employee is tricked via spear-phishing or deepfake/ACH invoice fraud into voluntarily wiring money or handing over credentials.
policy_clauses.contract_standard: Most cheap cyber add-ons cap Social Engineering at $10,000–$25,000. Enterprise MSAs demand a minimum $100,000–$250,000 sublimit.
